claim: Catalytically inactive enzyme paralogs occur in many genomes.
source: Catalytically inactive enzyme paralogs occur in many genomes.
evidence: This is a general statement about the prevalence of pseudoenzymes across genomes, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Some catalytically inactive enzyme paralogs regulate their active counterparts.
source: Some regulate their active counterparts but the structural principles of this regulation remain largely unknown.
evidence: This statement is supported by the general knowledge and citations discussed in the introduction.

claim: The structural principles of regulation by catalytically inactive enzyme paralogs remain largely unknown.
source: Some regulate their active counterparts but the structural principles of this regulation remain largely unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field at the time of the study.

claim: Monomeric TbAdoMetDC is inactive because of autoinhibition by its N-terminal sequence.
source: We show monomeric TbAdoMetDC is inactive because of autoinhibition by its N-terminal sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data from the TbAdoMetDCΔ26 crystal structure showing the N-terminal sequence blocking the active site.

claim: Heterodimerization with prozyme displaces the N-terminal autoinhibitory sequence from the active site through a mechanism involving cis-to-trans proline isomerization.
source: Heterodimerization with prozyme displaces this sequence from the active site through a complex mechanism involving a cis-to-trans proline isomerization, reorganization of a β-sheet, and insertion of the N-terminal α-helix into the heterodimer interface, leading to enzyme activation.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the monomer and heterodimer crystal structures showing P31 in cis-conformation in the monomer and trans-conformation in the heterodimer.

claim: Heterodimerization with prozyme involves reorganization of a β-sheet.
source: Heterodimerization with prozyme displaces this sequence from the active site through a complex mechanism involving a cis-to-trans proline isomerization, reorganization of a β-sheet, and insertion of the N-terminal α-helix into the heterodimer interface, leading to enzyme activation.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing β-strand slips and flips in the pyruvoyl β-sheet between monomer and heterodimer structures.

claim: Heterodimerization with prozyme involves insertion of the N-terminal α-helix into the heterodimer interface.
source: Heterodimerization with prozyme displaces this sequence from the active site through a complex mechanism involving a cis-to-trans proline isomerization, reorganization of a β-sheet, and insertion of the N-terminal α-helix into the heterodimer interface, leading to enzyme activation.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing helix h1 docked into the heterodimer interface in the active structure.

claim: The evolution of the intricate regulatory mechanism was facilitated by the acquisition of the dimerization domain.
source: We propose that the evolution of this intricate regulatory mechanism was facilitated by the acquisition of the dimerization domain, a single step that can in principle account for the divergence of regulatory schemes in the AdoMetDC enzyme family.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural analysis and phylogenetic comparison of AdoMetDC family members.

claim: Pseudoenzymes are estimated to represent up to 10% of human encoded proteins.
source: These 'pseudoenzymes' are estimated to represent up to 10% of human encoded proteins, and are particularly abundant within the protease and kinase families.
evidence: This is a cited estimate from the literature about the prevalence of pseudoenzymes.

claim: Pseudoenzymes are particularly abundant within the protease and kinase families.
source: These 'pseudoenzymes' are estimated to represent up to 10% of human encoded proteins, and are particularly abundant within the protease and kinase families.
evidence: This is a cited observation from the literature.

claim: Many enzymes form functional oligomers.
source: An interesting hypothesis emerges from the fact that many enzymes form functional oligomers (Goodsell and Olson, 2000; Marianayagam et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations.

claim: Pseudoenzymes might generally evolve to serve as regulators of enzymes by directly interacting with their cognate active homolog.
source: This property leads to the idea that pseudoenzymes might generally evolve to serve as regulators of enzymes, directly interacting with their cognate active homolog to exert regulatory control.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the oligomeric nature of many enzymes.

claim: Trypanosomatids encode inactive paralogs for two essential enzymes in the polyamine pathway.
source: Trypanosomatids encode inactive paralogs for two essential enzymes in the polyamine pathway (Willert et al., 2007; Willert and Phillips, 2008, 2012; Nguyen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The two essential enzymes with inactive paralogs in trypanosomatids are S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylase (AdoMetDC) and deoxyhypusine synthase.
source: These enzymes, S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylase (AdoMetDC) and deoxyhypusine synthase, have been characterized from Trypanosoma brucei, the causative agent of HAT.
evidence: This is stated explicitly and supported by citations.

claim: Both AdoMetDC and deoxyhypusine synthase are profoundly activated (~1000 fold increase in catalytic efficiency) by oligomerization with their paralogous pseudoenzyme.
source: Both enzymes are profoundly activated (~1000 fold increase in catalytic efficiency) by oligomerization with their paralogous pseudoenzyme leading to formation of catalytically functional complexes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: AdoMetDC is a pyruvoyl-dependent enzyme.
source: AdoMetDC is a pyruvoyl-dependent enzyme that catalyzes formation of decarboxylated AdoMet, a substrate required for biosynthesis of the polyamine spermidine from putrescine (Pegg, 2009b) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the enzyme mechanism, supported by citation.

claim: AdoMetDC catalyzes formation of decarboxylated AdoMet.
source: AdoMetDC is a pyruvoyl-dependent enzyme that catalyzes formation of decarboxylated AdoMet, a substrate required for biosynthesis of the polyamine spermidine from putrescine (Pegg, 2009b) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is the known enzymatic function, shown in Figure 1 and supported by citation.

claim: Decarboxylated AdoMet is a substrate required for biosynthesis of the polyamine spermidine from putrescine.
source: AdoMetDC is a pyruvoyl-dependent enzyme that catalyzes formation of decarboxylated AdoMet, a substrate required for biosynthesis of the polyamine spermidine from putrescine (Pegg, 2009b) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge shown in Figure 1 and supported by citation.

claim: Spermidine is essential in all eukaryotes for hypusine modification of the translation elongation factor eIF5A by deoxyhypusine synthase.
source: Spermidine is essential in all eukaryotes for hypusine modification of the translation elongation factor eIF5A by deoxyhypusine synthase (Dever et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The polyamine biosynthetic pathway has been targeted for development of anti-proliferative agents, including for the treatment of HAT.
source: As a consequence the polyamine biosynthetic pathway has been targeted for development of anti-proliferative agents, including for the treatment of HAT (Jacobs et al., 2011; Willert and Phillips, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The AdoMetDC pyruvoyl group plays a key role in the catalytic mechanism.
source: The AdoMetDC pyruvoyl group plays a key role in the catalytic mechanism and derives from an autocatalytic processing reaction that cleaves the peptide backbone into β- and α-chains (Pegg, 2009b; Bale and Ealick, 2010)(Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the enzyme mechanism, supported by citations.

claim: The AdoMetDC pyruvoyl group derives from an autocatalytic processing reaction that cleaves the peptide backbone into β- and α-chains.
source: The AdoMetDC pyruvoyl group plays a key role in the catalytic mechanism and derives from an autocatalytic processing reaction that cleaves the peptide backbone into β- and α-chains (Pegg, 2009b; Bale and Ealick, 2010)(Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established knowledge shown in Figure 2A and supported by citations.

claim: Trypanosomatid AdoMetDC undergoes autocatalytic cleavage to form the pyruvoyl cofactor.
source: Trypanosomatid AdoMetDC undergoes this cleavage, while the corresponding pseudoenzyme, which we call 'prozyme', lacks key residues and is not processed to the active form (Willert and Phillips, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Prozyme lacks key residues and is not processed to the active form.
source: Trypanosomatid AdoMetDC undergoes this cleavage, while the corresponding pseudoenzyme, which we call 'prozyme', lacks key residues and is not processed to the active form (Willert and Phillips, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Prozyme is only found in the trypanosomatids.
source: Prozyme is only found in the trypanosomatids.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and phylogenetic studies.

claim: The T. brucei AdoMetDC/prozyme complex is a heterodimer.
source: The T. brucei AdoMetDC/prozyme complex is a heterodimer, whereas T. brucei AdoMetDC (TbAdoMetDC) alone forms a homodimer only at high concentrations (Velez et al., 2013; Willert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous biochemical characterization.

claim: T. brucei AdoMetDC alone forms a homodimer only at high concentrations.
source: The T. brucei AdoMetDC/prozyme complex is a heterodimer, whereas T. brucei AdoMetDC (TbAdoMetDC) alone forms a homodimer only at high concentrations (Velez et al., 2013; Willert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: Mutagenesis and biochemical data implicated the TbAdoMetDC N-terminus in the prozyme-induced activation mechanism.
source: Mutagenesis and biochemical data implicated the TbAdoMetDC N-terminus in the prozyme-induced activation mechanism, but the structural basis for the regulation was not elucidated (Velez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The polyamine biosynthetic pathway is highly regulated in most eukaryotic cells.
source: The polyamine biosynthetic pathway is highly regulated in most eukaryotic cells (Pegg, 2009a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Polyamine pathway regulatory mechanisms are not conserved in trypanosomatids.
source: However, these regulatory mechanisms are not conserved in trypanosomatids, and instead in T. brucei the pathway is regulated by prozyme through both allosteric (enzyme activation upon heterodimer formation) and protein expression effects that modulate the concentration of active AdoMetDC in the cell (Willert and Phillips, 2008; Xiao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In T. brucei the polyamine pathway is regulated by prozyme through both allosteric and protein expression effects.
source: However, these regulatory mechanisms are not conserved in trypanosomatids, and instead in T. brucei the pathway is regulated by prozyme through both allosteric (enzyme activation upon heterodimer formation) and protein expression effects that modulate the concentration of active AdoMetDC in the cell (Willert and Phillips, 2008; Xiao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Putrescine has been shown to stimulate both processing to form the pyruvoyl cofactor and enzyme activity in human AdoMetDC.
source: Some evidence for allosteric regulation has also been reported for human AdoMetDC where the polyamine putrescine has been shown to stimulate both processing to form the pyruvoyl cofactor and also enzyme activity (Pegg, 2009b; Bale and Ealick, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Putrescine stimulates the activity of monomeric TbAdoMetDC, though the effects are small in comparison to prozyme (10-fold versus 1000-fold).
source: Putrescine also stimulates the activity of monomeric TbAdoMetDC, though the effects are small in comparison to prozyme (10-fold versus 1000-fold) (Velez et al., 2013; Willert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: Trypanosomatid AdoMetDCs contain a highly conserved 16 amino acid N-terminal sequence that is not conserved in other species.
source: Trypanosomatid AdoMetDCs contain a highly conserved 16 amino acid N-terminal sequence that is not conserved in other species (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2.

claim: Deletion or mutation of the N-terminal 16 residues led to loss of prozyme-mediated activation of TbAdoMetDC despite competent heterodimer formation.
source: Deletion or mutation of these residues led to loss of prozyme-mediated activation of TbAdoMetDC despite competent heterodimer formation implicating the N-terminus in the activation mechanism (Velez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous mutagenesis studies.

claim: TbAdoMetDCΔ26 had low activity either as a monomer or after heterodimerization with prozyme.
source: Like the Δ16 mutant, TbAdoMetDCΔ26 had low activity either as a monomer or after heterodimerization with prozyme, and both were modestly (3-fold) more active in the presence of putrescine (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Table 1.

claim: TbAdoMetDCΔ26 was modestly (3-fold) more active in the presence of putrescine.
source: Like the Δ16 mutant, TbAdoMetDCΔ26 had low activity either as a monomer or after heterodimerization with prozyme, and both were modestly (3-fold) more active in the presence of putrescine (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Table 1.

claim: TbAdoMetDCΔ26 crystals diffracted to 1.48 Å resolution.
source: TbAdoMetDCΔ26 yielded crystals (space group P212121) that diffracted to 1.48 Å resolution (Table 2).
evidence: This is crystallographic data reported in Table 2.

claim: A single TbAdoMetDCΔ26 αβ-monomer was found in the asymmetric unit.
source: A single TbAdoMetDCΔ26 αβ-monomer was found in the asymmetric unit composed of a four-layer sandwich with two central β-sheets positioned between outer α-helices (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TbAdoMetDCΔ26 is composed of a four-layer sandwich with two central β-sheets positioned between outer α-helices.
source: A single TbAdoMetDCΔ26 αβ-monomer was found in the asymmetric unit composed of a four-layer sandwich with two central β-sheets positioned between outer α-helices (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The N-terminal β-sheet contains pyruvoyl at the N-terminus of β4 and is composed of residues from both the α- and β-chains.
source: The N-terminal β-sheet (strands β1-β8) contains pyruvoyl at the N-terminus of β4 (pyruvoyl β-sheet) and is composed of residues from both the α- and β-chains, whereas the C-terminal β-sheet (scaffolding β-sheet) contains only α-chain residues (strands β9-β16) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The C-terminal β-sheet (scaffolding β-sheet) contains only α-chain residues (strands β9-β16).
source: The N-terminal β-sheet (strands β1-β8) contains pyruvoyl at the N-terminus of β4 (pyruvoyl β-sheet) and is composed of residues from both the α- and β-chains, whereas the C-terminal β-sheet (scaffolding β-sheet) contains only α-chain residues (strands β9-β16) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 2C.

claim: No density consistent with a bound putrescine was observed in the structure of TbAdoMetDCΔ26.
source: To assess the contribution of putrescine to the TbAdoMetDC activation mechanism it was included in crystallization buffers. However, no density consistent with a bound putrescine was observed in the structure of TbAdoMetDCΔ26.
evidence: This is an observation from the crystal structure electron density maps.

claim: The inactivity of TbAdoMetDCΔ26 is explained by an autoinhibitory mechanism mediated by residues S27-G30, which block the active site.
source: The inactivity of TbAdoMetDCΔ26 is explained by an autoinhibitory mechanism mediated by residues S27-G30, which block the active site (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figures 2C-E.

claim: The G30-P31 peptide bond is in the cis-conformation in TbAdoMetDCΔ26.
source: The G30-P31 peptide bond is in the cis-conformation, orienting S27-G30 into the active site.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The cis-conformation of G30-P31 orients S27-G30 into the active site.
source: The G30-P31 peptide bond is in the cis-conformation, orienting S27-G30 into the active site.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: F28 is positioned within 3.8 Å of the pyruvoyl overlapping with the active site of HsAdoMetDC.
source: This configuration places F28 within 3.8 Å of the pyruvoyl overlapping with the active site of the previously reported HsAdoMetDC structure (Ekstrom et al., 1999) (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is structural data from comparison of TbAdoMetDCΔ26 with HsAdoMetDC structures.

claim: In HsAdoMetDC the equivalent peptide bond (HsG9-T10) is in the trans-conformation.
source: In contrast, the equivalent peptide bond in HsAdoMetDC (HsG9-T10) is in the trans-conformation, and the N-terminus extends away from the active site, positioning HsF7 (equivalent to TbF28) to form one wall of the substrate-binding site (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is structural data from the HsAdoMetDC structure.

claim: In HsAdoMetDC the N-terminus extends away from the active site, positioning HsF7 to form one wall of the substrate-binding site.
source: In contrast, the equivalent peptide bond in HsAdoMetDC (HsG9-T10) is in the trans-conformation, and the N-terminus extends away from the active site, positioning HsF7 (equivalent to TbF28) to form one wall of the substrate-binding site (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is structural data from the HsAdoMetDC structure.

claim: The TbAdoMetDCΔ26 autoinhibitory residues are well defined by electron density.
source: The TbAdoMetDCΔ26 autoinhibitory residues are well defined by electron density and form extensive interactions in the active site stabilizing the observed conformation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure electron density maps shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The autoinhibitory residues form extensive interactions in the active site stabilizing the observed conformation.
source: The TbAdoMetDCΔ26 autoinhibitory residues are well defined by electron density and form extensive interactions in the active site stabilizing the observed conformation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The autoinhibitory interactions include π-π-stacking between F28 and Y243.
source: These interactions include, π-π-stacking between F28 and Y243 and H-bonds between the side chain of E85 and the backbone amide of S27, and between the amide of G101 and the carbonyl of E29.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The autoinhibitory interactions include H-bonds between the side chain of E85 and the backbone amide of S27.
source: These interactions include, π-π-stacking between F28 and Y243 and H-bonds between the side chain of E85 and the backbone amide of S27, and between the amide of G101 and the carbonyl of E29.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The autoinhibitory interactions include H-bonds between the amide of G101 and the carbonyl of E29.
source: These interactions include, π-π-stacking between F28 and Y243 and H-bonds between the side chain of E85 and the backbone amide of S27, and between the amide of G101 and the carbonyl of E29.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: P31 is conserved throughout the trypanosomatid AdoMetDCs.
source: P31 is conserved throughout the trypanosomatid AdoMetDCs (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2.

claim: TbAdoMetDC/prozyme wild-type heterodimer was crystallized with putrescine both in the absence (apo-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme) and presence (CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme) of CGP 40215.
source: TbAdoMetDC/prozyme wild-type heterodimer was crystallized with putrescine both in the absence (apo-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme) and presence (CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme) of CGP 40215 (CGP), a known AdoMetDC inhibitor (Bacchi et al., 1996) (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the crystallization conditions.

claim: Crystals from both apo and CGP conditions diffracted to 2.4 Å.
source: Crystals (space group P21) from both conditions diffracted to 2.4 Å (Table 2).
evidence: This is crystallographic data reported in Table 2.

claim: Two TbAdoMetDC/prozyme heterodimers are observed per asymmetric unit.
source: Two TbAdoMetDC/prozyme heterodimers are observed per asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The two heterodimers are associated in a tetrameric structure formed partially through a domain swap involving prozyme β-strands.
source: They are associated in a tetrameric structure formed partially through a domain swap involving prozyme β-strands (β0'), but which buries a relatively small surface area (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The TbAdoMetDC/prozyme complex was previously shown to be a dimer in solution by analytical ultracentrifugation.
source: The TbAdoMetDC/prozyme complex was previously shown to be a dimer in solution by analytical ultracentrifugation (Velez et al., 2013; Willert et al., 2007), thus the tetramer is unlikely to be relevant to its catalytic function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous biochemical studies.

claim: The tetramer observed in the crystal is unlikely to be relevant to the catalytic function of TbAdoMetDC/prozyme.
source: The TbAdoMetDC/prozyme complex was previously shown to be a dimer in solution by analytical ultracentrifugation (Velez et al., 2013; Willert et al., 2007), thus the tetramer is unlikely to be relevant to its catalytic function.
evidence: This is an inference based on solution studies showing the complex is a dimer.

claim: Both apo- and CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structures contain ligands bound at identical sites between the β-sheets.
source: Both apo- and CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structures contain ligands bound at identical sites between the β-sheets (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structures shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In prozyme, the electron density is consistent with a bound putrescine.
source: In prozyme, the electron density is consistent with a bound putrescine (Put') (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C); however, in TbAdoMetDC the corresponding electron density is larger and the crystallization buffer bis-tris propane (B3P) was modeled into the site (Figures 1 and 3A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is structural data from electron density maps shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: In TbAdoMetDC the electron density at the ligand binding site is larger than putrescine and bis-tris propane (B3P) was modeled into the site.
source: In prozyme, the electron density is consistent with a bound putrescine (Put') (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C); however, in TbAdoMetDC the corresponding electron density is larger and the crystallization buffer bis-tris propane (B3P) was modeled into the site (Figures 1 and 3A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is structural data from electron density maps shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structure has CGP bound in the active site.
source: The CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structure additionally has CGP bound in the active site and a second putrescine (Put) found in a novel site near the N-terminal α-helix (h1) (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structure has a second putrescine found in a novel site near the N-terminal α-helix (h1).
source: The CGP-TbAdoMetDC/prozyme structure additionally has CGP bound in the active site and a second putrescine (Put) found in a novel site near the N-terminal α-helix (h1) (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Prozyme and TbAdoMetDC subunits share the same overall fold.
source: Prozyme and TbAdoMetDC subunits share the same overall fold (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is structural data from comparison of the two subunits shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Prozyme is missing the pyruvoyl cofactor.
source: However, besides the pyruvoyl, prozyme is also missing additional active site residues including the ligand-binding residue Y243, helices h9-h11 and strand β10.
evidence: This is structural data from the prozyme structure.

claim: Prozyme is missing the ligand-binding residue Y243.
source: However, besides the pyruvoyl, prozyme is also missing additional active site residues including the ligand-binding residue Y243, helices h9-h11 and strand β10.
evidence: This is structural data from the prozyme structure.

claim: Prozyme is missing helices h9-h11 and strand β10.
source: However, besides the pyruvoyl, prozyme is also missing additional active site residues including the ligand-binding residue Y243, helices h9-h11 and strand β10.
evidence: This is structural data from the prozyme structure.

claim: The TbAdoMetDC/prozyme dimer interface contains an extensive buried surface area (3,200 Å2).
source: The TbAdoMetDC/prozyme dimer interface contains an extensive buried surface area (3,200 Å2).
evidence: This is structural data calculated from the crystal structure.

claim: Strands β9-β16 form a scaffold that extends across the dimer interface with H-bond interactions formed between β15 from TbAdoMetDC (R336-E340) and β15' from prozyme (R305-H309).
source: Strands β9-β16 form a scaffold that extends across the dimer interface with H-bond interactions formed between β15 from TbAdoMetDC (R336-E340) and β15' from prozyme (R305-H309) (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Additional interface interactions are observed between AdoMetDC pyruvoyl β-sheet (β7 and h8) and prozyme loop β7'-β8', and vice versa.
source: Additional interface interactions are observed between AdoMetDC pyruvoyl β-sheet (β7 and h8) and prozyme loop β7'-β8', and vice versa.
evidence: This is structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: Heterodimerization is likely initiated by the formation of the extended β-sheet across the dimer interface between the structurally rigid scaffolding β-sheet of TbAdoMetDC and its counterpart in prozyme.
source: Heterodimerization is likely initiated by the formation of the extended β-sheet across the dimer interface between the structurally rigid scaffolding β-sheet of TbAdoMetDC and its counterpart in prozyme (Figure 3D), providing a platform to support the conformational changes required for activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The structural reorganization upon heterodimerization is defined by three segments of movement: repositioning of the autoinhibitory residue and N-terminal h1 helix, reorganization of the pyruvoyl β-sheet, and ordering of the β6-h8 connector loop.
source: The structural reorganization is defined by three segments of movement: (1) repositioning of the autoinhibitory residue and N-terminal h1 helix, (2) reorganization of the pyruvoyl β-sheet, and (3) ordering of the β6-h8 connector loop (Figure 4 and Video 1).
evidence: This is structural data from comparison of monomer and heterodimer structures shown in Figure 4 and Video 1.

claim: In the TbAdoMetDC/prozyme heterodimer, the autoinhibitory residues (S27-G30) have been displaced from the active site.
source: Firstly, in the TbAdoMetDC/prozyme heterodimer, the autoinhibitory residues (S27-G30) have been displaced from the active site, which relieves the autoinhibition and positions F28 to form the catalytically competent ligand-binding site (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is structural data from the heterodimer structure shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Displacement of the autoinhibitory residues relieves the autoinhibition and positions F28 to form the catalytically competent ligand-binding site.
source: Firstly, in the TbAdoMetDC/prozyme heterodimer, the autoinhibitory residues (S27-G30) have been displaced from the active site, which relieves the autoinhibition and positions F28 to form the catalytically competent ligand-binding site (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is structural data from the heterodimer structure shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Displacement of the autoinhibitory residues is facilitated by cis-to-trans isomerization of P31.
source: This movement is facilitated by cis-to-trans isomerization of P31.
evidence: This is structural data from comparison of monomer and heterodimer structures.

claim: The TbAdoMetDC N-terminal α-helix (h1, residues S7-R19) docks into the heterodimer interface stabilizing the open conformation of the active site.
source: The TbAdoMetDC N-terminal α-helix (h1, residues S7-R19) then docks into the heterodimer interface stabilizing the open conformation of the active site (Figures 3A, 4A and 5A).
evidence: This is structural data from the heterodimer structure shown in Figures 3A, 4A and 5A.

claim: The formation of the h1 binding site is accompanied by rearrangement of the pyruvoyl β-sheet.
source: Secondly, the formation of the h1 binding site is accompanied by rearrangement of the pyruvoyl β-sheet (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is structural data from comparison of monomer and heterodimer structures shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The scaffolding β-sheets and connecting coils and helices (TbAdoMetDC residues Tb189-356) align closely between the heterodimer and monomer structures (RMSD of 1.1 Å for 168 equivalent Cα atoms).
source: While the scaffolding β-sheets and connecting coils and helices (TbAdoMetDC residues Tb189-356) align closely between the heterodimer and monomer structures (RMSD of 1.1 Å for 168 equivalent Cα atoms), the β-chain and α-chain residues Tb87-179 forming the pyruvoyl β-sheet and connecting coils and helices show significant deviations (RMSD of 5.1 Å for 145 equivalent Cα atoms) (Figure 4C,D).

evidence: This is an inference based on sequence analysis.

claim: The allosteric mechanism in eukaryotic AdoMetDC enzymes likely arose through the acquisition of the dimerization domain.

evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.
